chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him)
That the Commander of the Faithful (peace be upon him) disliked the partnership of the Jew, the Christian, and the Magian, 'unless it is a present trade' in which one does not absent oneself.

key_terms.أَمِيرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ: Commander of the Faithful (Ali ibn Abi Talib)
key_terms.التِّجَارَة الْحَاضِرَة: Present trade (active partnership where partners are present)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on partnership with People of the Book in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from *Tahdhib al-Ahkam* clarifies the conditions under which Imam Ali (AS) permitted commercial partnerships with People of the Book, distinguishing between general social or financial entanglement and specific, transparent transactions. The exception of 'present trade' (*tijarah hadirah*) implies a partnership where the partner remains actively involved and visible, ensuring accountability and preventing the ambiguity or potential deceit associated with absent partners. This ruling reflects the Shia juristic principle of balancing social coexistence with the preservation of religious and economic integrity.
